stages.title: Run hosted compiler CI when a review wave becomes ready
stages.problem: Publishing many complete draft prerequisites can launch every expensive compiler matrix simultaneously.
stages.example: A draft PR keeps its captured local validation; marking it ready triggers the host and device compiler jobs through ready_for_review.
stages.design: Keep normal push and PR checks, but skip compiler jobs while the PR is draft and explicitly listen for ready_for_review.
stages.tradeoffs: Drafts have no hosted compiler result; skipped jobs must not be described as passing. Local intermediate checks remain required before publication.

stages.title: Bound template-build concurrency and cancel stale CI revisions
stages.problem: Launching one compiler per hosted CPU can exhaust memory once formatting templates grow; stale runs consume the same runner quota.
stages.example: On a runner with many CPUs, make -j2 bounds compiler processes while a newer PR commit cancels the superseded workflow.
stages.design: Set a consistent two-job compile bound and a workflow/PR concurrency key without reducing the compiler matrix.
stages.tradeoffs: Less parallelism may increase wall time. Cancelled stale runs are incomplete evidence, not passing checks.

stages.title: Pin the shared fmt oracle to an immutable revision
stages.problem: System format implementations and moving oracle revisions can disagree about expected output.
stages.example: For a subnormal double, every portable test compares the same ffmt bytes with the same fmt revision on every compiler.
stages.design: Pin the Make reference before introducing the independent oracle and new focused comparisons; retain an explicit external FMT_DIR override.
stages.tradeoffs: Expected behavior follows this fixed fmt revision rather than the installed standard library; updating it requires an explicit compatibility review.
stages.docs: docs/contributing/ORACLE.md

stages.title: Register portable capability tests without silently omitting sources
stages.problem: Discovering test source files with a wildcard can silently omit a declared test when its file is missing.
stages.example: A registration naming test/conformance/test_output.cpp is a required Make prerequisite; deleting that source fails the build rather than shrinking the test suite.
stages.design: Each capability adds a small explicit registration. A shared Make fragment provides compiler, reference-library, C++ standard and optional-extension handling.
stages.tradeoffs: Registrations are additional build metadata, but independent feature branches add separate files and do not edit one combined test source or suite list.
stages.docs: docs/contributing/TESTS.md

stages.title: Report source-file region, executable-line and branch coverage
stages.problem: One-header region percentages omit new headers and cannot describe executable-line or branch-edge coverage.
stages.example: Two headers with a region at the same coordinates remain two regions; an unexecuted branch side stays uncovered.
stages.design: Include source filenames in union keys, preserve any-instantiation coverage, and read executable lines from LLVM LCOV export rather than estimating spans.
stages.tradeoffs: Only instantiated runtime code is measured. Device-only code, compile-time evaluation and uninstantiated templates remain outside the denominator. This PR preserves the blocking policy.
stages.docs: Coverage metrics can accept a file or header directory. This measurement extension does not relax the existing regression gate; policy is reviewed separately.

stages.title: Replace the blocking coverage regression gate with reporting
stages.problem: Header movement and template instantiation alter the coverage denominator, so aggregate percentage decreases can block a behavior-preserving change.
stages.example: Before: a 0.02 percentage-point drop fails CI. After: valid per-file base/head JSON is uploaded and the same drop is visible but does not block merging.
stages.design: Keep invalid or empty measurement blocking, report region/line/branch metrics across all library headers, and make per-file regression assessment a human review decision.
stages.tradeoffs: This deliberately loses automatic detection of real percentage regressions. Passing CI no longer guarantees nondecreasing coverage; correctness and sanitizer checks remain independent blocking checks.

stages.title: Capture exact subprocess bytes and terminate timed-out children
stages.problem: Compiler drivers can spawn children that outlive a timeout; text decoding can erase output distinctions.
stages.example: compare_bytes(b"value\n", b"value") reports a mismatch; an embedded NUL remains observable.
stages.design: Keep byte capture, process lifetime and evidence-path handling in one small reusable module; save both streams before returning.
stages.tradeoffs: Timeout cleanup uses POSIX process groups; its regression is explicitly skipped where killpg is unavailable.
stages.docs: Process results preserve raw stdout/stderr, exit status, command arguments and elapsed time. Timeout cleanup kills the complete compiler process group.

stages.title: Require intended diagnostics in negative compilation tests
stages.problem: Treating every failed compilation as a rejected format lets missing headers and compiler crashes pass.
stages.example: A consteval invalid-format diagnostic passes; "fmt/format.h: No such file or directory" is an infrastructure failure.
stages.design: Compile a positive control and syntax-only fixture before testing both ffmt paths and fmt. Classify diagnostics independently of the differential runner.
stages.tradeoffs: Compiler diagnostic recognition is a conservative heuristic, not a compiler-independent proof; unfamiliar wording fails visibly.
stages.docs: Negative compilation requires the intended format diagnostic. Infrastructure failures, unrelated errors and unexpected acceptance fail the check.

stages.title: Compare host output with an independently compiled fmt oracle
stages.problem: The legacy test harness can share assumptions with the implementation; expected bytes need an independent formatting implementation.
stages.example: A standalone fmt process formats INT64_MIN; a separate ffmt process must produce the identical bytes.
stages.design: Compile fmt only into host reference executables, and compile ffmt targets without fmt headers. Require a clean checkout at the exact oracle pin without modifying it, and record format.h/format.cc hashes. Begin with four baseline cases supported before engine migration.
stages.tradeoffs: Separate reference and target compilation reduces shared assumptions but costs compile time. Dirty or differently pinned oracle checkouts fail visibly. Accelerator routes and later feature cases arrive in independent changes.
stages.docs: The host differential runner compiles the pinned fmt oracle independently. The reference checkout must be clean, and exact format.h/format.cc hashes are retained; verification never changes the caller checkout. Feature fixture modules are introduced with implementations; every loaded fixture file receives a source hash.

stages.title: Verify benchmark output before collecting timing samples
stages.problem: Fast timing numbers are meaningless if the candidate truncates output or executes a different workload.
stages.example: Before measuring integer memory formatting, compare its emitted verification bytes with a separate pinned fmt executable.
stages.design: Snapshot sources and benchmark primitives, require a clean pinned fmt oracle, compare output before timing, validate sample counts and checksums, and retain exact commands and source hashes.
stages.tradeoffs: Host wall timing includes launch and synchronization for accelerators. Verification process time and first batch are recorded separately; neither is a cold-JIT claim.
stages.docs: Output verification precedes timing. Manifests retain source snapshots, runner files, exact compiler commands and timer policy; campaign conclusions belong in ffmt-evaluation.

stages.title: Add explicit memory and printing benchmark primitives
stages.problem: Formatting into memory and printing have different costs; a reusable benchmark must preserve that distinction.
stages.example: Integer memory mode formats value={:+012d} into a bounded buffer; print mode emits the same presentation through the selected transport.
stages.design: Keep the callable primitive, single-process sampling harness and optional second translation unit directly reviewable as handwritten C++.
stages.tradeoffs: These primitives define workloads, not hardware conclusions. Five warmups and thirty samples do not make first invocation a cold-JIT measurement.
stages.docs: Memory and print modes are separate workload primitives. Input values are exact binary fractions; shortest conversion is compared with fmt in memory only.

stages.title: Retain compiler resource reports independently of timing measurements
stages.problem: Object size, static compiler frame size, accelerator scratch and registers describe different resources and must not be conflated with measured runtime.
stages.example: --resources-only compiles one- and two-call probes and preserves the compiler report without claiming device execution.
stages.design: Keep raw tool output, object hashes and backend image metadata beside parsed resource fields; distinguish compile-only probe outcomes from timing rows.
stages.tradeoffs: Tool availability and diagnostic wording vary. Static frame reports exclude cumulative call depth; linked-image and conversion-table sizes are separate measurements.
stages.docs: Resource probes are compile-only evidence. Compiler frames, scratch, registers, retained tables and image sizes are named separately and retain raw commands and diagnostics.

stages.title: Share explicit compiler target selection between execution adapters
stages.problem: CUDA, HIP and OpenMP launchers need the same target-selection rules without importing each other.
stages.example: FFMT_GPU_ARCH=sm_80 selects sm_80 without consulting nvidia-smi.
stages.design: Isolate architecture discovery behind two small functions; prefer explicit environment overrides and retain existing fallback targets.
stages.tradeoffs: Fallback targets support compilation without a device, but do not prove execution compatibility. Execution controls remain required.
stages.docs: Set FFMT_GPU_ARCH explicitly when a compiler target differs from the first visible device. Target discovery is a compiler default, not execution evidence.

stages.title: Add independent CUDA differential execution adapter
stages.problem: CUDA source compilation needs compiler-specific language and architecture flags, and successful compilation alone cannot establish that a kernel executed.
stages.example:
--route cuda selects Clang CUDA; --route nvcc selects NVIDIA nvcc.
Both launch one execute_case(index) kernel, check launch/synchronization errors,
and require FFMT_DEVICE metadata before comparing stdout bytes.
stages.design: Keep both CUDA compiler routes in one handwritten runtime adapter. Probe device availability, record the selected device, launch one thread, and synchronize before the process exits.
stages.tradeoffs: The common fixture stays free of fmt device code. These Python tests inspect the generated source and flags; a CUDA device/runtime is still required to establish execution.
stages.docs: Run a literal case in a one-thread CUDA kernel through nvcc or Clang. Execution requires a CUDA device and runtime; Python checks only source generation here.

stages.title: Add independent HIP differential execution adapter
stages.problem: HIP and chipStar share a launch API but need different compiler flag choices; a failed launch must not be mistaken for a formatting mismatch.
stages.example:
--route hip uses hipcc with the selected ROCm offload architecture.
--route chipstar uses the externally selected HIP runtime.
Both check hipLaunchKernelGGL, the last launch error and device synchronization.
stages.design: Use one handwritten HIP runtime adapter for the two compiler routes. Keep architecture selection on the native HIP route, and retain device properties and launch failures as separate evidence.
stages.tradeoffs: The caller supplies the appropriate hipcc/runtime environment. Portable tests check source generation and flag overrides; they do not execute a HIP or chipStar kernel.
stages.docs: Run the same case through a HIP kernel without a fmt device build. Execution requires the selected HIP or chipStar runtime and a device.

stages.title: Preserve failed batches before isolating individual cases
stages.problem: A combined switch can fail although individual cases succeed, and retrying without saving it erases the failure.
stages.example: When a two-case binary crashes, save its source hash and diagnostic before retrying one-case binaries.
stages.design: Require a positive execution control, recursively split failed build batches, and isolate remaining cases after runtime failures. Save each checkpoint atomically.
stages.tradeoffs: Retries increase compile time and isolated passes do not erase batch failures. A failed control produces not_run outcomes, not a formatting judgment.
stages.docs: Failed batch builds and executions remain in manifest shard_failures before per-case isolation. Positive controls separate missing execution capability from formatting outcomes.

stages.title: Add independent KOKKOS differential execution adapter
stages.problem: A Kokkos installation can select a different DefaultExecutionSpace from the route requested by a test, producing a misleading backend result.
stages.example:
--route kokkos-cuda requires DefaultExecutionSpace::name() == "Cuda".
A Serial installation returns 77 before formatting, rather than being reported
as a successful CUDA comparison.
stages.design: Wrap the existing base compiler adapter with Kokkos includes/link flags, require the requested execution space, run one parallel_for, and fence before finalization. Advertise an accelerator wrapper only when its base adapter is present.
stages.tradeoffs: Kokkos must be installed externally with the requested execution space. Source-generation tests cover the guard, launch and lifecycle, while runtime/device availability remains unqualified here.
stages.docs: Only advertise kokkos-cuda when the CUDA base adapter is present. Kokkos must be installed externally with the selected execution space; no site profiles are included.

stages.title: Execute numeric memory records through the CUDA adapter
stages.problem: CUDA stdout can succeed while numeric conversion or bounded output counts in accelerator memory are wrong.
stages.example:
cudaMemcpyHostToDevice -> memory_kernel -> cudaDeviceSynchronize
-> cudaMemcpyDeviceToHost -> serialize(input, output)
stages.design: Allocate CUDA input/output buffers, copy input encodings, zero output, launch memory_kernel, check errors/synchronize, and copy framed results back. The numeric formatting body remains the shared handwritten template.
stages.tradeoffs: Runtime execution remains hardware-dependent; source-generation and host record tests validate structure but do not establish accelerator execution.
stages.docs: The memory launcher formats on the selected backend and copies records to the host for byte-exact oracle comparison. Stdout control failure does not hide memory outcomes.

stages.title: Execute numeric memory records through the HIP adapter
stages.problem: HIP stdout can succeed while numeric conversion or bounded output counts in accelerator memory are wrong.
stages.example:
hipMemcpyHostToDevice -> hipLaunchKernelGGL -> hipDeviceSynchronize
-> hipMemcpyDeviceToHost -> serialize(input, output)
stages.design: Allocate HIP input/output buffers, copy input encodings, zero output, launch with hipLaunchKernelGGL, check errors/synchronize, and copy framed results back. The same adapter also serves the chipStar route.
stages.tradeoffs: Runtime execution remains hardware-dependent; source-generation and host record tests validate structure but do not establish accelerator execution.
stages.docs: The memory launcher formats on the selected backend and copies records to the host for byte-exact oracle comparison. Stdout control failure does not hide memory outcomes.

stages.title: Execute numeric memory records through the KOKKOS adapter
stages.problem: Kokkos stdout can succeed while numeric conversion or bounded output counts in accelerator memory are wrong.
stages.example:
host mirror -> deep_copy(device_input) -> parallel_for(format_record)
-> create_mirror_view_and_copy(HostSpace, device_output) -> serialize
stages.design: Require the requested DefaultExecutionSpace, deep-copy input through a host mirror, format into a device View with parallel_for, and copy a HostSpace mirror back before serialization and finalization.
stages.tradeoffs: Runtime execution remains hardware-dependent; source-generation and host record tests validate structure but do not establish accelerator execution.
stages.docs: The memory launcher formats on the selected backend and copies records to the host for byte-exact oracle comparison. Stdout control failure does not hide memory outcomes.

stages.title: Execute numeric memory records through the OPENMP adapter
stages.problem: OpenMP stdout can succeed while numeric conversion or bounded output counts in accelerator memory are wrong.
stages.example:
omp_is_initial_device() must be false
map(to: input[0:count]) + map(from: output[0:count])
-> format_record on the target -> serialize copied records
stages.design: Require non-initial-device execution, map input encodings to the target and output records from it, then format each record in a target teams distribute parallel for region.
stages.tradeoffs: Runtime execution remains hardware-dependent; source-generation and host record tests validate structure but do not establish accelerator execution.
stages.docs: The memory launcher formats on the selected backend and copies records to the host for byte-exact oracle comparison. Stdout control failure does not hide memory outcomes.

stages.title: Execute numeric memory records through the SYCL adapter
stages.problem: SYCL stdout can succeed while numeric conversion or bounded output counts in accelerator memory are wrong.
stages.example:
GPU queue: memcpy(input) -> memset(output) -> parallel_for(format_record)
-> memcpy(output) -> serialize(input, output); every stage waits and reports exceptions
stages.design: Use a GPU queue and explicit device USM allocations. Wait on input copies, zeroing, parallel_for and output copies with wait_and_throw before freeing memory and serializing results.
stages.tradeoffs: Runtime execution remains hardware-dependent; source-generation and host record tests validate structure but do not establish accelerator execution.
stages.docs: The memory launcher formats on the selected backend and copies records to the host for byte-exact oracle comparison. Stdout control failure does not hide memory outcomes.

stages.title: Compare bounded numeric memory records with host fmt output
stages.problem: Printf transport can hide whether floating-point conversion and bounded output accounting produced the correct memory bytes.
stages.example: A record for a subnormal double checks the input encoding, output bytes, written/required counts and error status against independent fmt.
stages.design: Use explicit binary framing and a fixed seed. Keep numeric operations in a conventionally formatted handwritten C++ template that is hashed with runner inputs.
stages.tradeoffs: The default corpus has 4096 seeded float encodings, 4096 seeded double encodings, and 24 boundary/special encodings. This is representative sampling, not exhaustive floating-point proof. The portable smoke command reduces the seed count to 32 per type and executes host memory only.
stages.docs: The numeric memory suite checks byte payloads, framing, input bits, written and required sizes, and error status. The template is handwritten source, not excluded generated material. Raw record framing is unchanged from the preserved suite.

stages.title: Add independent OPENMP differential execution adapter
stages.problem: OpenMP target regions can silently run on the initial host device, allowing a host result to masquerade as accelerator conformance.
stages.example:
--route omp-cuda / omp-hip use Clang NVPTX / AMDGPU offload flags.
--route omp-spirv uses icpx -fiopenmp -fopenmp-targets=spir64.
An initial-device control returns 77 before any output case is judged.
stages.design: Share one target-region launcher across the three compiler routes, require omp_is_initial_device() to be false, record the device number, and keep route-specific flags beside the launcher.
stages.tradeoffs: Host fallback becomes a failed execution control, not a formatting pass. Portable tests inspect source generation and flags; they do not establish an available OpenMP device runtime.
stages.docs: Reject an OpenMP target region that executes on the initial host device. Execution requires a working offload toolchain and accelerator; host fallback is failure.

stages.title: Compare invalid literal rejection against the independent oracle
stages.problem: Matching valid output does not establish that an implementation rejects malformed or type-incompatible format literals.
stages.example: The unclosed "{" fixture must produce an intended format diagnostic in both the target compiler and the host fmt oracle.
stages.design: Reuse the diagnostic classifier for revisioned negative fixture modules and preserve both compiler diagnostics separately.
stages.tradeoffs: This adds compile-time rejection parity, not runtime parser exception parity. The baseline fixture registry has no new negative cases until engine migration.
stages.docs: Revisioned negative fixtures accompany parser behavior and run through both the independent host fmt oracle and the selected target compiler.

stages.title: Qualify immutable headers from an independent source checkout
stages.problem: Re-running a comparison against a moving worktree can silently change the source under test.
stages.example: --source-root ../ffmt --revision COMMIT snapshots that commit even when its working headers have subsequent edits.
stages.design: Snapshot include/ through git archive for pinned revisions, or copy current headers for WORKTREE; identify runner checkout separately from library checkout.
stages.tradeoffs: Only headers belong to the library snapshot. Exact runner/fixture hashes and compiler commands remain separate evidence, not an assertion of a clean worktree.
stages.docs: --revision COMMIT snapshots immutable headers. --source-root CHECKOUT separates the tested library checkout from the portable runner; manifests retain both revisions and all captured hashes.

stages.title: Add independent SYCL differential execution adapter
stages.problem: SYCL implementations may select different devices, and asynchronous kernel errors need to be observed before stdout comparison.
stages.example:
--route sycl uses icpx -fsycl; --route acpp uses AdaptiveCpp generic targets.
The launcher requests sycl::gpu_selector_v, records the device name/fp64 support,
and waits with wait_and_throw() before judging output.
stages.design: Keep Intel SYCL and AdaptiveCpp compiler flags in one handwritten SYCL adapter. A mandatory GPU selector and explicit exception-aware wait prevent CPU fallback or pending errors from looking like a formatting pass.
stages.tradeoffs: The caller supplies a working SYCL GPU runtime. Python tests check selection, launch/wait structure and flag overrides; accelerator execution is not qualified here.
stages.docs: Use a GPU selector, launch one SYCL task, and retain its device name. Execution requires SYCL or AdaptiveCpp GPU support; a CPU fallback cannot pass.

stages.title: Count bounded output independently of formatting
stages.problem: Truncation must retain the complete required length without writing beyond caller capacity.
stages.design: All iterator copies share a sink. Required-length overflow is detected before arithmetic wraps.
stages.tradeoffs: Counts describe code units, not display columns; family alignment hooks arrive with shared family support.

stages.title: Extract the qualified compiler configuration
stages.problem: The standalone checked engine needs the same compiler and backend configuration as the qualified implementation.
stages.example: #include <ffmt/detail/config.hpp>
stages.design: Compiler macros and standard includes are copied without changes from aeff043. The extraction hash records the exact body.
stages.tradeoffs: This header is internal; callers continue including base.hpp. It does not activate the replacement engine.

stages.title: Isolate the qualified decimal conversion helpers
stages.problem: The qualified conversion routines were embedded in the public base header.
stages.example: // Existing handwritten bodies move into detail/dragonbox.hpp and detail/exact_decimal.hpp.
stages.design: Bodies are copied unchanged from aeff043. Only namespace and OpenMP-region wrappers are added; extraction hashes are recorded.
stages.tradeoffs: The helpers are not activated until conversion integration. Handwritten logic remains explicitly handwritten.

stages.title: Preserve the existing implementation behind a wrapper
stages.problem: The replacement engine needs independent qualification while current callers remain usable.
stages.example: #include <ffmt/base.hpp> // still selects the original implementation
stages.design: The legacy header is copied byte for byte from upstream 3fe258a; the public wrapper only selects it.
stages.tradeoffs: The temporary extra include is removed once migration is validated.

stages.title: Preserve native long-double and binary128 representations
stages.problem: Passing extended values through double loses range and precision before formatting.
stages.design: Native 80-bit and 128-bit decomposition feeds the same exact decimal algorithm. Formatting does not require quadmath conversion.
stages.tradeoffs: Layouts and availability are target dependent. Unsupported representations return a checked status.
stages.source_changes: Test-only binary128 guard enables FMT_USE_FLOAT128 before the oracle include only when FFMT_HAS_FLOAT128 is true; unsupported compilers still compile the return77 branch. Formatter logic is unchanged.

stages.title: Format native 128-bit and bit-precise integers
stages.problem: Standard type traits do not consistently recognize native extended integers.
stages.design: Explicit signed and unsigned traits preserve the native width. _BitInt support follows the oracle surface through 64 bits.
stages.tradeoffs: Compiler extensions are conditional. Wider _BitInt values report unsupported rather than narrowing.
stages.source_changes: Native extension test now returns77 when int128 is unavailable, so absence is recorded as skip rather than a passing empty test. Formatter logic is unchanged.

stages.title: Convert binary floating values with bounded integer storage
stages.problem: Device environments cannot consistently provide host conversion services.
stages.design: Representation bits drive classification and exact interval comparisons. Bounded integer limbs hold decimal expansions without output-capacity limits.
stages.tradeoffs: Integer interval conversion uses more code and bounded working storage than forwarding to libc, while avoiding locale and allocation services. Internal conversion renders supported finite magnitudes; the formatting layer handles signs and nonfinite spellings. The documented 1100/16520-digit bounds cover exact IEEE expansions and interval endpoints, rather than limiting requested output precision. Direct oracle tests cover adjacent powers of two, subnormal/normal transitions, maximum finite values, rounding ties and carries.

stages.title: Format float and double with exact presentation rules
stages.problem: Floating fields need correct rounding even when requested precision exceeds stored output.
stages.design: Shortest formatting uses Dragonbox normally and integer interval conversion for fast-math and SPIR-V. Requested trailing zeros stream through counted sinks.
stages.tradeoffs: The oracle stays strictly compiled. Host fast-math tests use separately established expected strings and do not qualify device runtimes.

stages.title: Map user values through ADL format_as
stages.problem: Small wrappers should reuse primitive formatting without a full formatter specialization.
stages.design: ADL mapping participates in parsing, output and dynamic width validation. Values retain references until mapping occurs.
stages.tradeoffs: Mappings terminate at primitive representations; they are not a recursive serialization interface.

stages.title: Support parse/context formatters and correct forwarding
stages.problem: User-defined values need to consume specs and write into the caller context.
stages.design: Eligibility checks inspect the cv-qualified reference accepted by format. Shared sink iterators preserve nested counts without copying user objects.
stages.tradeoffs: The protocol is template based with checked statuses; it does not provide exception services or type-erased stores.

stages.title: Adapt the existing static formatter protocol
stages.problem: Existing ffmt formatters return a literal and a tuple from static format functions.
stages.design: Legacy values expand through the counted engine. Narrow nested literals are converted for wide destinations without allocating.
stages.tradeoffs: Legacy custom formatters accept empty specs; modern parse/context formatters remain the spec-aware interface.

stages.title: Select the checked engine through the public header
stages.problem: The separately qualified engine must replace both old output paths while preserving API spellings.
stages.example:
#include <ffmt/base.hpp>
auto result = ffmt::try_print("{:04x}", 42);
stages.design: The public wrapper selects the same engine tested throughout this stack. Existing macros, static formatters and built-in SYCL formatters remain available.
stages.tradeoffs: Void compatibility calls discard checked status. Host checks do not replace preserved accelerator campaign evidence.
stages.source_changes: Restore all aeff historical suite migrations: oracle output is no longer truncated to staging capacity; null strings are checked for rejection; both compatibility routes test shortest floats and fast-math subnormals. These are restored qualified test behaviors, not new formatter algorithms.

stages.title: Delete the retired formatter implementation
stages.problem: The public header no longer references the old implementation after migration.
stages.example: #include <ffmt/base.hpp> // unchanged for callers
stages.design: Only the unused legacy implementation is deleted; archived snapshots retain it for comparison.
stages.tradeoffs: The static formatter protocol and legacy emit-hook adapter remain supported by the new implementation.

stages.title: Parse and validate counted format strings
stages.problem: Runtime execution and literal validation need a single grammar.
stages.design: A handler receives parsed fields; parse context tracks index modes and checks dynamic references without producing output.
stages.tradeoffs: This prefix supports ASCII fill; counted Unicode decoding is introduced with its tests.

stages.title: Format primitive values into bounded memory
stages.problem: The old print-only interface cannot safely target caller-owned memory or report the full required size.
stages.design: Builtin formatters share one parser and counted sink. Signs, base prefixes, padding and digits have separate output responsibilities.
stages.tradeoffs: Floating, Unicode display rules and customization protocols are introduced separately.

stages.title: Deliver counted bytes through host and accelerator stdout
stages.problem: Long output and percent signs must reach stdout without reinterpretation as format syntax.
stages.design: A bounded sink emits counted chunks. Backend printf uses fixed conversion formats; compatibility hooks receive safe escaped pieces.
stages.tradeoffs: Some backend or legacy transports cannot preserve embedded NULs and report errors. Host captures validate contracts, not accelerator runtime behavior.
reading_order: test/capture.hpp:raw stream equality after parsed diagnostics
stages.source_changes: Preserve original byte-counted transport and restore aeff raw stdout equality regression in the legacy capture helper. Portable legacy-host checks ensure this stricter harness remains valid before migration.

stages.title: Apply counted Unicode decoding and display rules
stages.problem: Byte counts alone misalign multibyte text, and decoding must respect counted boundaries.
stages.design: Counted UTF-8 decoding, display-width tables and printability tables govern fill, alignment, precision and debug escapes. Wide output follows code-unit semantics.
stages.tradeoffs: These are qualified fmt semantics, not terminal-specific grapheme measurement. Unicode can still be disabled explicitly.

stages.title: Format durations, calendar values and time points
stages.problem: Format chrono values without host locale, timezone-database or strftime services.
stages.design: Civil-date arithmetic and explicit tokens preserve device callability; locale/timezone queries remain unsupported.
stages.tradeoffs:
The header supports durations, C++20 calendar values, `std::tm`, system time
points and local time points using civil-date arithmetic and explicit tokens.
Fractional precision, negative timestamps and ISO week years follow the pinned
fmt reference. This implementation provides locale-independent formatting; it
does not query clocks, a timezone database or locale services. Local time points
therefore reject zone/offset tokens. Device use requires the involved standard
chrono operations to be available on that device.

source_provenance.source_changes: Conventional header layout; duration/calendar/token/wide/rejection tests grouped, oracle calendar wrappers kept local. No implementation token change.

stages.before: A std::chrono::milliseconds value has no formatter, so the %T token cannot produce a duration.

validation.results: Pending validation of the assembled intermediate commit; root records exact commands and outcomes.
validation.limitations: Portable checks do not establish accelerator runtime availability. No hardware campaign rerun is warranted by whitespace/comments, helper renaming and test decomposition alone.

stages.title: Opt enums into integer formatting
stages.problem: Expose enum underlying values without globally accepting every enum.
stages.design: Small ADL opt-in shares the integer parser and avoids symbolic-name reflection.
stages.tradeoffs:
`ffmt::underlying(value)` explicitly exposes an enum's underlying integer.
Opting into `ffmt::enums::format_as` in the enum's namespace enables ADL mapping
with the integer formatter's specifications. This prints integer values rather
than discovering symbolic names. The opt-in avoids globally making every enum
formattable.

source_provenance.source_changes: Conventional header layout; enum-specific tests/docs extracted from omnibus. No implementation token change.

stages.before: An enum with no formatter or ADL mapping cannot be passed directly to checked formatting.

validation.results: Pending validation of the assembled intermediate commit; root records exact commands and outcomes.
validation.limitations: Portable checks do not establish accelerator runtime availability. No hardware campaign rerun is warranted by whitespace/comments, helper renaming and test decomposition alone.

stages.title: Test names with independent range and standard adapters
stages.problem: Verify cross-feature composition without making optional adapters depend on each other.
stages.design: Integration-only fixtures sit above independent feature branches.
stages.tradeoffs:
Named argument wrappers preserve the referenced family's mutability and provide
runtime names for outer width fields. The interaction tests combine names with
ranges and standard-type adapters. Each family and named arguments also has an
independent test suite, so this integration adds no prerequisite between those
features.

source_provenance.source_changes: Only existing named-range, named-complex and mutable named-range interaction tests moved into a dedicated suite. No library implementation source.

stages.before: Independent names/ranges/std suites do not verify named widths on optional adapters or mutable named ranges.

validation.results: Pending validation of the assembled intermediate commit; root records exact commands and outcomes.

stages.title: Add referenced named arguments
stages.problem: Resolve human-readable field names while retaining typed value references.
stages.design: Name lookup is runtime; wrappers do not allocate or own their referents.
stages.tradeoffs:
`ffmt::arg(name, value)` stores a name view and a value reference. The name
characters and value must outlive use of the wrapper; temporary values remain
valid through the formatting expression. Names and named width/precision fields
are resolved at runtime. Literal parsing checks structural syntax, but cannot
fully validate a named field's type/specification because names are runtime data.
Use checked results to observe unresolved names or incompatible specifications.

source_provenance.source_changes: Borrowing/lifetime comments and conventional header layout; decomposed named tests plus direct missing-name, incompatible-spec and invalid-width status regressions. No implementation token change.

stages.title: Format ranges, tuples and joins
stages.problem: Format structured containers using element formatters while preserving iterator semantics.
stages.design: Range detection and constrained formatter specializations; standard operations remain device-dependent.
stages.tradeoffs:
Ranges select sequence, set, map, string or debug-string presentation. Tuples
and container adaptors have explicit adapters; nested specifications follow the
second colon, while `n` removes delimiters. `range_format_kind` customizes string
versus debug-string treatment. Joins hold iterator/delimiter views; keep their
underlying objects alive. Mutable and move-only input iterators are preserved.
Right/center alignment on streaming iterators requires repeatable element
formatters and forward ranges; bounded writable buffers handle consuming ranges
without replay. The standard-library operations used by the range must be
callable on the selected device.

source_provenance.source_changes: Conventional header layout; range/iterator/mutation tests extracted and grouped, cross-feature named-range assertion moved to integration. No implementation token change.

stages.title: Share nested output accounting and family alignment
stages.problem: Optional formatters need consistent nested alignment without buffering or replaying mutations.
stages.design: Extend bounded sink iterators with padding marks/reordering and delegate hooks, then share family outer parsing and one-pass accounting. Streaming destinations explicitly require replayable values for right/center alignment.
stages.tradeoffs:
The internal helpers share outer alignment parsing, display-column accounting,
debug defaults and nested formatting. Left-aligned output renders once on any
iterator. Bounded writable pointer buffers also support right/center alignment
in one pass by inserting padding while retaining the exact truncated prefix.
Other iterators require replayable values for right/center alignment; unknown
custom formatters and consuming ranges return `unsupported_type` before invoking
the formatter. These helpers are implementation details, not a public extension
API. Optional formatters should document which input operations are device callable.

stages.title: Adapt standard value wrappers and complex numbers
stages.problem: Format common standard wrappers through existing contained-value formatters.
stages.design: Explicit adapters avoid streams and RTTI; each standard operation must be available on the target.
stages.tradeoffs:
Optional and variant values use debug presentation for contained text; bitsets,
bytes, reference wrappers, atomics, complex numbers, source locations and pointer
views have explicit adapters. `ffmt::ptr` makes a raw/smart pointer printable
without dereferencing it. Atomic formatting loads the current value; a format
call is not an atomic snapshot across multiple arguments. These adapters do not
supply filesystem, streams, RTTI, thread-ID or exception-traversal services.
Standard-library types and their operations must themselves be device callable.

source_provenance.source_changes: Conventional header layout; wrapper/bitset/complex/pointer/rejection tests extracted and grouped. No implementation token change.

stages.title: Format C++23 expected and unexpected values
stages.problem: Represent expected values and errors when the standard library supports C++23.
stages.example:
#include <ffmt/std23.hpp>
ffmt::println("{}", std::expected<int, int>{42}); // expected(42)
stages.design: Keep expected/unexpected adapters in an opt-in header. Make excludes suites declaring c++23 from its default capability target and exposes test-cxx23 explicitly; CMake retains its independent opt-in option.
stages.tradeoffs:
`std23.hpp` adds `std::expected` and `std::unexpected` adapters when the selected
standard library exposes C++23 expected support. C++20 users can omit the header.
The contained value and error must be formattable. Optional tests report skip
(exit 77) when the standard library lacks the feature; that skip is not evidence
of conformance. Enable the suite with a C++23 compiler mode.

source_provenance.source_changes: Conventional header/test layout and standalone C++23 suite name; every expected/unexpected fixture retained. No implementation token change.

stages.title: Add explicit ANSI color and emphasis wrappers
stages.problem: Request ANSI styling explicitly around an existing formattable value.
stages.example:
#include <ffmt/color.hpp>
ffmt::println("{}", ffmt::styled(42, ffmt::fg(ffmt::rgb(255,20,30)) | ffmt::emphasis::bold));
stages.design: Typed composition emits deterministic bytes without terminal detection.
stages.tradeoffs:
Styles explicitly emit ANSI escape bytes around the formatted value and reset
when a nonempty style ends. There is no terminal detection; captured output also
contains those bytes. RGB, terminal palette colors and emphasis flags compose
with `operator|`. Incompatible repeated terminal colors report `invalid_format`.
The wrapped formatter still owns ordinary value parsing and width semantics.

stages.title: Add checked typed percent formatting
stages.problem: Support percent formatting without unsafe C varargs or the writing conversion %n.
stages.design: A separate typed grammar shares primitive conversion and bounded sinks, but does not implement %n.
stages.tradeoffs:
The percent parser uses typed arguments rather than C varargs and shares the
bounded output/error contract of brace formatting. It supports positional
arguments, dynamic width/precision, integer length modifiers and narrow/wide
output. Invalid conversions report errors; `%n` is rejected and never writes
through a pointer. Floating arguments follow printf's float-to-double promotion.
This parser is intentionally separate from brace parsing so each grammar can be
reviewed and tested independently.

source_provenance.source_changes: Conventional header layout; all percent-format matrices/arguments/guards retained in named test groups. No implementation token change.
